 Criminial Petition No.10505 of 2023

sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner, to direct the XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally,
Hyderabad to complete the trial as expeditiously as possible in C.C.No.15061 of 2019.

entities.text:
XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner; learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
3.

It is the specific contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that a complaint has been made by respondent No.2 against petitioner herein contending that he has been introduced to one Mr.Bipin Jain (the petitioner herein) by one of his trusted person and accordingly he started dealing with him with the sales of gold bullion and ornaments which were carried out with proper bills and payments against cheque/DD/RTGS and he had smooth transaction and hence gained confidence against the petitioner.

4. In the month of October, 2016, the petitioner promised to get gold for better price and asked him to make payment of Rs.8,50,00,000/- and since he could not deliver the goods inturn issued two cheques as the payments for the same.
Further the said cheques were dishonoured by the Bank.

Secondly, the petitioner has taken gold biscuits from the complainant against delivery challan for a value of Rs.9,00,00,000/- against which he issued a cheque of HDFC Bank without date and promised to clear the cheque and was been absconding.
Basing on the above, a case was registered against the petitioner and police after due investigation has laid charge sheet for the offence punishable under Section 420 I.P.C.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner filed the present petition.

5. It is the specific contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that entire ingredients clearly disclose that facts come under Section 138 of N.I.Act and therefore it is a fit case for the petitioner to succeed in the trial Court and prayed this Court to direct the trial Court to complete the trial in C.C.No.15061 of 2019 as expeditiously as possible.

6. Without going into the merits of the case, this Court is of the considered view that as Calendar Case is of the year 2019 and even after a lapse of 4 years the trial Court has not disposed of the same,
and further taking into consideration that it is one of the oldest cases of the said Court and there are only 11 witnesses to examine in this case, therefore, XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Nampally, Hyderabad is directed to dispose of the C.C.No.15061 of 2019 within a period of four (4) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
7. With the above directions, this criminal petition is disposed of, accordingly.
